s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion
salient_findings: 3-month history of painless swelling in the right upper posterior tooth region
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Ground-glass trabecular pattern with radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars on radiographs
key_facts: 9-year-old boy presented with a facial swelling
Swelling is located in the right upper posterior tooth region
Swelling has grown progressively over 3 months
Swelling is painless
Swelling has caused facial asymmetry
Medical and family histories are unremarkable
Examination revealed a 4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling
Overlying skin is normal
Intraorally, there is a 4.0×3.0 cm ovoid, hard, nontender swelling in the right buccal vestibule
Buccal cortical expansion and slight palatal expansion are present
No mucosal changes are present
Radiographs show a ground-glass trabecular pattern with radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars
Cone-beam CT reveals expansion of the buccal and palatal cortical plates

differentials: Ossifying fibroma of the sinonasal tract
per_call: Ossifying fibroma of the sinonasal tract

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical and radiological findings of a progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion and a ground-glass appearance

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a ground-glass trabecular pattern, although the well-defined margin makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to the presence of a painless facial swelling with bony expansion, although the age and location are not typical

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to juvenile ossifying fibroma, with a possible consideration due to the radiological findings

shortlist.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: A broad category that includes juvenile ossifying fibroma and fibrous dysplasia, and is consistent with the clinical and radiological findings

raw.rationale: The well-defined margin of the swelling and the ground-glass internal pattern on radiographs are characteristic of juvenile ossifying fibroma, which is further supported by the patient's age and the location of the swelling in the posterior maxilla.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Ill-defined margin and merging with surrounding areas are typical of fibrous dysplasia, which contradicts the well-defined margin observed in this case.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Bilateral involvement and a typical 'cherubic' appearance are characteristic of cherubism, which does not match the unilateral presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: The radiographic appearance and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest cemento-ossifying fibroma, which often presents with a more mixed radiolucent and radiopaque pattern.

rejected.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes juvenile ossifying fibroma, but the specific characteristics of the case point more directly to juvenile ossifying fibroma as the most likely diagnosis.
